name: Scrape TikTok hashtags and sounds by engagement with Bright Data, GPT-5.6, Google Sheets and Slack

parameters.content:
## Find the TikTok hashtags and sounds that actually earn engagement

Give it a few topics and it comes back with the tags and sounds whose posts beat the median for that topic, each with the numbers behind it and the content format that goes with it.

### How it works
A weekly schedule sends one TikTok search per topic through Bright Data's discovery API. It takes a minute or two, so the workflow uses the asynchronous API properly: it triggers the search, then polls the snapshot on a Wait loop with a five-minute cap until the rows are ready.

Every post gets an engagement rate of likes, comments, shares and saves over plays. Posts are then grouped by hashtag and by sound, and each group is compared with the median engagement of its own topic, so a busy niche cannot outrank a quiet one. Reach tags like fyp and viral are dropped because every account in every niche uses them, and a tag on fewer than three posts is left out rather than measured. GPT-5.6 reads the captions of each tag's best posts and names the content format behind it.

TikTok search ranks on relevance rather than date, so the digest states how old the posts are instead of calling anything a trend. Tags reported recently are skipped for thirty days, the whole list lands in Google Sheets, and a ranked digest goes to Slack.

### Setup
Add a Bright Data API key as a Header Auth credential (`Authorization` / `Bearer YOUR_KEY`), connect OpenAI, Google Sheets and Slack, then set your topics and channel in Set Topic Config.

### Customization
Raise min_lift for a shorter, stronger list, or raise min_posts_per_tag so a tag needs more posts behind it before it counts.

## 1. Pick the topics
A few TikTok searches on a weekly schedule. Everything you would tune lives in one config node.

## 2. Search TikTok asynchronously
Bright Data runs one search per topic. Eight posts took 82 seconds in testing, so this polls the snapshot until the rows are ready.

## 3. Measure tags, not posts
Every post gets an engagement rate, then hashtags and sounds are compared with the median of their own topic. Reach tags like fyp are dropped.

## 4. Drop the ones you have had
The sheet doubles as the do-not-repeat list, so a tag reported recently stays out of this week's digest.

## 5. Name the format behind the tag
The model reads the captions of each tag's best posts and answers in English. Every number stated as fact comes from a field.

## 6. Deliver
One sheet row per tag, which is what the next run reads back, plus a ranked Slack digest.

## These are not trends
TikTok search returns what is relevant, not what is new - test posts came back months old. Lift is measured against the same search's own median.
